trials.hypothesis: The observed target is the design shifted X/2 columns with wrap-around. Feed the network both the raw input and a copy shifted back by X/2 (built only from slices and concatenation), so every channel has a copy lined up with the build and the action grid. Its first 1x1 learned layer can then compare target and build at each cell. Expect dev success clearly above 0 and placements made instead of instant DONE. Refuted if it still collapses to DONE at about 0 success.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.shift = int(spec.X) // 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(2 * spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        k = self.shift
        rolled = torch.cat([obs[:, :, :, k:], obs[:, :, :, :k]], dim=3)
        inp = torch.cat([obs, rolled], dim=1)
        s = self.stem(inp)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.label: r1c2
trials.name: All x-shifts, learned pick
trials.hypothesis: A general fix that does not assume the shift is X/2. Stack copies of the input at every wrap-around x-shift (0..X-1) before the first learned 1x1 layer, so the network can learn which shift lines the target up. It costs about 25% more compute, so fewer samples. If it roughly matches the fixed X/2 shift, this is a robust recipe for other world sizes. Refuted if it stays near 0 while the fixed shift succeeds.

import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)

            nn.Conv2d(2 * spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())

        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)

        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

        rolled = torch.cat([obs[:, :, :, k:], obs[:, :, :, :k]], dim=3)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"ppo_epochs": 2, "ent_coef": 0.02, "n_minibatches": 16, "gamma": 0.99, "gae_lambda": 0.95}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.shift = int(spec.X) // 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(2 * spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        k = self.shift
        rolled = torch.cat([obs[:, :, :, k:], obs[:, :, :, :k]], dim=3)
        inp = torch.cat([obs, rolled], dim=1)
        s = self.stem(inp)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)

    return Net(spec)

COL = 48

PROJ = 32

        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

        res = []

trials.name: Landing-layer mixture head
trials.hypothesis: New head: for each layer z, apply a learned per-layer embedding, then ReLU, footprint pooling and a mixer whose weights are shared across layers. This gives a score for 'the brick lands at z and fills only missing cells'. The placement logit is the logsumexp over z. Splitting the decision by landing layer should make upper and overhanging placements easier to learn. Uses about 15% more compute and the r1c3 recipe. import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"ppo_epochs": 2, "ent_coef": 0.02, "n_minibatches": 16}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 16
HID = 16


class LayerHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, nz, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.nz = int(nz)
        self.np = proj
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.zemb = nn.Embedding(self.nz, proj)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        B, _, Y, X = f.shape
        p = self.proj(f)
        e = self.zemb.weight.view(1, self.nz, self.np, 1, 1)
        pz = F.relu(p.unsqueeze(1) + e).reshape(B * self.nz, self.np, Y, X)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = pz, pz, pz
            else:
                q = F.pad(pz, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            o = out(h).view(B, self.nz, Y, X)
            res.append(torch.logsumexp(o, dim=1))
        return torch.stack(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.shift = int(spec.X) // 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(2 * spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = LayerHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, spec.Z, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        k = self.shift
        rolled = torch.cat([obs[:, :, :, k:], obs[:, :, :, :k]], dim=3)
        inp = torch.cat([obs, rolled], dim=1)
        s = self.stem(inp)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"ppo_epochs": 2, "ent_coef": 0.02, "n_minibatches": 16}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class UnfoldHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix1 = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(proj * (dy * dx + 1), hid, 1) for dy, dx in self.fps])
        self.mix2 = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        Y = p.shape[2]
        X = p.shape[3]
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), m1, m2, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix1, self.mix2, self.outs):
            q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            parts = []

                    parts.append(q[:, :, i:i + Y, j:j + X])
            mx = parts[0]
            for t in parts[1:]:
                mx = torch.maximum(mx, t)
            h = F.relu(m1(torch.cat(parts + [mx], dim=1)))
            h = F.relu(m2(h))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)

        super().__init__()
        self.shift = int(spec.X) // 2

            nn.Conv2d(2 * spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())

        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = UnfoldHead(WIDTH + COL, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

        k = self.shift

        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)

analyses.1: The start network gave up straight away: every greedy episode is an immediate DONE, and the learning curve shrinks to length 1. The traces show why. The target heights the agent observes are the real design shifted 4 columns along x, wrapping round (X/2). Every row of both diagnostic designs matches this; it is not a mirror image. So the target sits in the wrong place compared with the build and the action grid. Small local convolutions cannot connect a cell to the cell 4 columns away, so placements look random, rewards are negative, and DONE (reward 0) wins. The missing/extra channels may be shifted too, since the agent learned nothing from them. The top priority is lining the target back up. This round tests: (1) a fixed shift back by X/2, (2) a general version that gives the first learned layer every x-shift and lets it pick, (3) the fixed shift plus a recipe that collects more samples and explores more, to resist the DONE collapse.
analyses.2: The observed target is the design shifted X/2 columns with wrap-around. Lining the target back up with the build fixed the collapse to DONE. With that fix, dev success was 0.59 on the default recipe and 0.63 with r1c3's recipe (ppo_epochs 2, which gives about 1.9x the samples). Seed spread is about ±0.14, so these two results are not clearly different. Learning a pick among all x-shifts also worked (0.44), so the method should carry over to other grid sizes. Training success was still rising at the end of every run, which suggests the agent is short of samples. In both diagnostic traces the agent fills the ground layer and layer 1 correctly, then chooses DONE while upper cells near rows 1–2, columns 1–2 are still missing. That points to two likely problems: the agent undervalues the +1 exact-build bonus, which gamma 0.95 discounts heavily, and its 5x5 receptive field is too small for upper layers and overhangs. Each training run took about 60 of the 900 seconds allowed, so time is not a constraint.
analyses.3: The observed target is shifted X/2 columns with wrap-around. Unrolling it fixed the instant-DONE collapse (0.59–0.63). Seed noise is large: r1c3's seeds scored 0.49 and 0.77, so gaps under about 0.15 mean little. ppo_epochs 1 (0.08) and gamma 0.99 (0.11) clearly hurt, even with similar gradient steps, so reusing data across epochs matters. The deeper trunk's collapse is confounded by its 1-epoch recipe. The traces show the agent filling layer 0 well, then saying DONE before placing upper or overhanging bricks (for example the 1x2 at layer 2 in design 1). Training success was still rising at the end, and there are only about 55 policy updates. Next: (1) twice as many smaller updates with the same samples per minibatch; (2) feed crisp per-cell stem features into the footprint head; (3) a new head that scores every possible landing layer z with shared weights and combines them with logsumexp.
analyses.4: Lining the shifted target up with the build was the key fix: the X/2 shift-back took dev success from 0 to about 0.6. Passing the per-cell stem features into the footprint head (r3c2) gave the best result, 0.70 (seeds 0.50 and 0.90), but that gain is within seed noise. Seed spread is very large. Moving the recipe away from ppo_epochs 2 with the default gamma did worse: 1 epoch, gamma 0.99 and 2x more updates all scored lower, and a deeper trunk collapsed to instant DONE. Training success was still rising at the end of every good run. In r3c2's trace the agent stops before placing one 1x2 overhang brick that needs exact per-cell landing reasoning, which pooled max/min/mean features lose. Two cheap levers remain: more gradient steps on the same samples (smaller minibatches add no counted compute), and a head that sees each footprint cell's features separately.
